title: Why Visitors Leave a Local Business Website

cover.alt: Concept illustration of a website maze with blocked visitor paths beside one clear route to a contact doorway.

figures.title: Review the visitor's path
figures.summary: Look for friction at each stage of reaching and understanding the business.

items.label: Arrival
items.detail: Check image weight, unnecessary scripts, and mobile loading behavior.

items.label: Understanding
items.detail: Make the service, audience, and area clear in the first screen.

items.label: Using the page
items.detail: Test readable text, comfortable taps, and reflow on a phone.

items.label: Finding proof
items.detail: Show authentic work, relevant credentials, and attributable reviews.

items.label: Making contact
items.detail: Keep contact details and the intended action easy to find.

figures.caption: A qualitative review framework from the article, not a measured conversion result.

figures.title: Start with three practical checks
figures.summary: The article prioritizes loading, clarity, and a reachable contact action.

items.label: Reduce unnecessary weight
items.detail: Compress images and review scripts that do not support the visitor's task.

items.label: Clarify the headline
items.detail: State what the business does and whom it serves.

items.label: Make contact obvious
items.detail: Show a usable phone link and a straightforward alternative contact route.

items.label: Verify the result
items.detail: Test the actual phone experience and observe whether the intended tasks work.

figures.caption: A suggested improvement sequence. Measure your own site before drawing conclusions about visitor behavior.
